key_insight: A superconducting transmon qubit can deterministically and programmatically generate multipartite entangled mechanical states across multiple phonon modes, including W, GHZ, and cluster states.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable control strategy for compact multimode mechanical platforms that could enable quantum simulation, sensing, and information storage on chip.
method: Sequentially apply optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and selected mechanical modes.
Prepare matrix product states with bond dimension two in a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator.
Use quantum state tomography to certify the generated entangled states and probe correlated-noise sensing behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports full characterization by tomography, genuine multipartite entanglement certification across up to four modes, and quantitative bounds on collective dephasing from W/GHZ decoherence comparisons.
watch_item: Scalability will depend on maintaining high-fidelity qubit-mode control and managing decoherence as the number of mechanical modes increases.
paper_title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
